== 1. a chained command (compose stops at &&)
verdict: wrong (3 claims checked, 0 hold, 3 wrong)
WRONG command: cd /app && npm start [stringRunsInShell]
-> `web`'s `command:` runs no shell: compose splits it into words and stops at `&&`, dropping `&& npm start`, so the command is `cd
/app`. To run all of it, start a shell: `command: ["sh", "-c", "cd /app && npm start"]`.
WRONG Compose runs `command` through a shell, so `web` runs `cd /app && npm start`. [stringRunsInShell]
-> Compose runs no shell for a `command:` or `entrypoint:` string: it splits the string into words and stops at the first unquoted `;`,
`&`, `|`, `<` or `>`. Shell features need `sh -c`.
WRONG Compose runs `command` through a shell, so `web` runs `cd /app && npm start`. [stringRunsInShell]
-> `web` runs the image's ENTRYPOINT, then `cd /app`: compose runs no shell for a `command:` string; it splits the string into words and
stops at `&&`, dropping `&& npm start`.
== 2. the fix: a shell started on purpose
verdict: verified (2 claims checked, 2 hold)
holds Compose does not run a `command` string through a shell, so the list starts one: `web` runs `cd /app && npm start`.
holds Compose does not run a `command` string through a shell, so the list starts one: `web` runs `cd /app && npm start`.
== 3. a guide's explanation of the same bug
verdict: wrong (1 claim checked, 0 hold, 1 wrong)
WRONG In `docker-compose.yml`, a string `command` is split into words without a shell, so `&&` is passed to the program as a literal argument.
[operatorBecomesArgument]
-> Compose does not pass `&&` (or `;`, `|`, `>`) to the program: it stops reading the string there and drops the rest.
== 4. a variable set only in environment:
verdict: wrong (3 claims checked, 0 hold, 2 to check, 1 wrong)
caution command: echo $GREETING
-> `greeter`'s `command:` uses `$GREETING`, which compose fills from your shell or `.env` when it reads the file, not from the service's
`environment:`; unless one of them sets it, the value is empty. For the container's value, write `$$GREETING` and run the command
through `sh -c`.
caution `$GREETING` becomes `hello`, because compose expands variables in `command` from the `environment:` block.
-> This holds only if your shell or `.env` sets `$GREETING` the same way: compose fills them when it reads the file and never reads
`greeter`'s `environment:`.
WRONG `$GREETING` becomes `hello`, because compose expands variables in `command` from the `environment:` block. [variableReadInContainer]
-> Compose substitutes `$NAME` in `command:` when it reads the file, from the shell running `docker compose` and `.env`; the service's
`environment:` is not used. `$$NAME` passes a literal `$NAME` for a shell in the container.
== 5. adding tini through entrypoint:
verdict: wrong (2 claims checked, 0 hold, 2 wrong)
WRONG Setting `entrypoint` keeps the image's `CMD`, so `app` runs `/sbin/tini -- node server.js`. [entrypointKeepsImageCmd]
-> Setting `entrypoint:` in compose drops the image's CMD; only `command:` gives the new entrypoint arguments.
WRONG Setting `entrypoint` keeps the image's `CMD`, so `app` runs `/sbin/tini -- node server.js`. [entrypointKeepsImageCmd]
-> `app` runs `/sbin/tini --`: an entrypoint set in compose drops the image's CMD (`node server.js`).
== 6. docker compose run, right and wrong
verdict: wrong (2 claims checked, 1 hold, 1 wrong)
holds `docker compose run --rm web npm test` runs `npm test`: the arguments after the service replace its `command`.
WRONG With `docker compose run --rm web npm test`, the container runs `npm run dev npm test`. [runAppendsToCommand]
-> `docker compose run --rm web npm test` runs the image's ENTRYPOINT, then `npm test`: the arguments after the service replace its
`command:`; they are not added to it.
== 7. sh -c handed its script in pieces
verdict: wrong (2 claims checked, 0 hold, 2 wrong)
WRONG command: echo ready [scriptTakesFollowingWords]
-> `worker` runs `sh -c echo ready`: `-c` takes only `echo` as the script, and `ready` only fills `$0`, `$1`, .... Put the script in one
word: `["sh", "-c", "echo ready"]`.
WRONG `worker` runs `echo ready` through `sh -c`. [scriptTakesFollowingWords]
-> `worker` runs `sh -c echo ready`: `-c` takes only the next word as the script; the words after it fill `$0`, `$1`, ...
